scope: Read-only integration review of in-progress core implementation against the committed Worker protocol; does not replace native or end-to-end test evidence.

findings.finding: Complete map page metadata is top-level http_cache; decoding only nested page omitted the validator base.
findings.resolution: Parent copies the top-level metadata into the page before decode_read and rejects disagreement when both copies are present.

findings.finding: Collecting the latest expired robots denial while older pinned rules remain could expose old validators after retention.
findings.resolution: Parent retains the newest decision until older rows can be removed, then collects the remaining singleton in a bounded additional pass.

findings.finding: Core rejected years before 1601 while Worker canonical date checking could accept earlier dates, turning a complete read into a protocol failure.
findings.resolution: Worker now uses the same lower year bound; 97 conditional tests passed, including two new old-date cases.

findings.finding: A failed refresh with nofollow but no noindex/nosnippet can change document_publication without a publication generation tracked by publication_history_locked; a later headerless 304 could recover snapshot follow_allowed and old links.
findings.requested_verification: Add failed-refresh nofollow -> headerless 304 -> crawl-frontier regression, and preserve the effective current follow restriction for 304 if confirmed.

positive_checks: cached_robots selects the newest decision first and only then checks freshness; it does not skip a newer denial to admit old allowed content.
304 page commit checks owner/current snapshot/body/cache metadata identity and preserves the original body publication and site-generation boundaries.
Map 304 validates request/byte usage and robots decision, and rebuilds only retained, bounded complete discovery links.
Profile-only configuration changes remove conditions before the original GET; malformed bindings or unsupported 304 never trigger a retry.
